content.text:
Absolutely. If you want the **closest “I just finished *The Expanse* and need more” hit**, I’d start here:

## 1. **_Revelation Space_ by Alastair Reynolds**
Dark, huge-scale space opera with ancient alien mysteries, hard-ish science, and a very cold universe. It’s less “found family crew banter” than *The Expanse*, but it scratches the **protomolecule / unknowable ancient tech / humanity is not ready** itch hard. It’s very commonly recommended for *Expanse* readers. ([bookrecommendationgenerator.com](https://bookrecommendationgenerator.com/books-to-read-after-the-expanse-series/?utm_source=openai))

## 2. **_A Fire Upon the Deep_ by Vernor Vinge**
If you loved the way *The Expanse* widens from solar-system politics into something much bigger, this is a great next step. It’s more mind-bending and far-future, but it has big stakes, fascinating alien intelligence, and serious momentum. ([best-sci-fi-books.com](https://best-sci-fi-books.com/24-books-like-the-expanse/?utm_source=openai))

## 3. **_Red Mars_ by Kim Stanley Robinson**
For the **realistic colonization, factions, engineering, and political struggle** side of *The Expanse*, this is probably the canonical pick. It’s slower and denser than Corey, but if you loved Mars/Belt/Earth tensions, this is very much in the same conversation. ([subspacesignals.com](https://www.subspacesignals.com/blog/best-sci-fi-books-for-fans-of-the-expanse?utm_source=openai))

## 4. **_The Collapsing Empire_ by John Scalzi**
More accessible, faster, funnier, and more political. Not as gritty as *The Expanse*, but it has interstellar infrastructure, scheming elites, and a civilization-threatening scientific problem. Good if you want a palate cleanser that still feels like space opera. ([screenrant.com](https://screenrant.com/sci-fi-books-read-like-the-expanse-list/?utm_source=openai))

## 5. **_Ancillary Justice_ by Ann Leckie**
If you liked Avasarala-level politics and big imperial power structures, this is excellent. It’s more literary and stranger in voice than *The Expanse*, but the worldbuilding is sharp and the revenge/conspiracy thread gives it real drive. ([bookshabit.com](https://bookshabit.com/books-to-read-after-the-expanse/?utm_source=openai))

## 6. **_Memory’s Legion_ by James S. A. Corey**
If you haven’t read the Expanse novellas/short stories yet, don’t skip this. It collects the short fiction set in the universe, including stories tied to major characters and events. It’s the obvious “one more drink at the Rocinante bar” choice. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory%27s_Legion?utm_source=openai))

**My pick for you:**  
If you want **closest vibe**, read **_Revelation Space_**.  
If you want **politics + realism**, read **_Red Mars_**.  
If you want **fast, fun, space-opera momentum**, read **_The Collapsing Empire_**.
